questions.question: Who among the following wrote ‘Nirmala’?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following wrote ‘Nirmala’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Munshi Premchand.

Key Points

  • 'Nirmala' is a famous novel written by Munshi Premchand, one of the most celebrated authors in Hindi literature.
  • The novel was published in 1925 and addresses critical issues like dowry and the plight of women in Indian society.
  • Premchand's writing style in 'Nirmala' is characterized by its realism, focusing on the socio-economic struggles of the time.
  • Munshi Premchand is widely regarded as the 'Upanyas Samrat'
  • He has written numerous other masterpieces, including 'Godaan', 'Karmabhoomi', and 'Sevasadan'.

Additional Information

  • Dowry System: The dowry system, which plays a central role in 'Nirmala,' refers to the practice of transferring parental property or wealth to a daughter at her marriage. It has been a critical social issue in India.
  • Realism in Literature: Premchand's works are known for their realism, portraying the struggles of the common man and highlighting social injustices and economic disparities.
  • Hindi Literature Evolution: Munshi Premchand significantly contributed to the evolution of Hindi literature by transitioning it from romanticism to addressing real-life social and economic issues.
  • Munshi Premchand's Legacy: He is celebrated not only in Hindi literature but also in Urdu literature, where he began his writing career before switching to Hindi.
  • Impact of 'Nirmala': The novel continues to be a subject of academic and literary discussion due to its progressive portrayal of women's issues and its critique of societal norms.

questions.question: Who was the author of the three-act play, 'Post Office'?
questions.questionHtml: Who was the author of the three-act play, 'Post Office'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

Key Points

  • Rabindranath Tagore was the author of the three-act play, 'Post Office' of 1912.
  • It concerns Amal, a child confined to his adoptive uncle's home by an incurable disease. 
  • W. Andrew Robinson and Krishna Dutta note that the play "continues to occupy a special place in Tagore's reputation, both within Bengal and in the wider world." It was written in four days.

Additional Information

  • Rabindranath Tagore:
    • He was the recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913 and is internationally known as a great poet. He was born in the year 1861, in Calcutta, Bengal.
    • From his earliest days, Rabindranath grew up in a house where all the changes emerging in Indian society of that time were being felt in his day-to-day life. Tagore's Philosophy of Education: Tagore, laid great stress and emphasis on the aesthetic development of the senses in his philosophy of education.
    • He argued that the development of the senses was as important as intellectual development. He, therefore, gave prominence to music, literature, art, dance, and drama in the daily life of the school.
    • Tagore believed in the all-around development of personality and in his institution education continues to address the all-around development of the students.
    • Tagore's theory of education is marked by naturalistic & aesthetic values. He had a belief that "The widest road leading to the solution of all our problems is education."
    • Education can develop a new pattern of life that culminates in the realization of a universal man. Tagore's system of education emphasizes the intellectual, physical, social, moral economic, and spiritual aspects of human life by which a man can develop an integrated personality.
    • Tagore believed that along with education, economic upliftment is also necessary.

questions.question: ‘A Passage to India’, a novel about the British Empire, was written by which of the following authors?
questions.questionHtml: ‘A Passage to India’, a novel about the British Empire, was written by which of the following authors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is EM Forster.

Key Points

  • EM Forster was a renowned English novelist, short story writer, and essayist.
  • "A Passage to India" was published in 1924 and is one of Forster's most famous works.
  • The novel explores the racial tensions and prejudices during the British rule in India.
  • Forster's other notable works include "Howards End" and "A Room with a View".

Additional Information

  • British Empire in India
    • The British Empire in India, also known as the British Raj, lasted from 1858 to 1947.
    • During this period, India was under the direct rule of the British Crown following the rebellion of 1857.
    • The British Raj had significant social, economic, and political impacts on India, including the introduction of English education, legal systems, and infrastructure development.
    • The period was also marked by significant resistance and movements for Indian independence, which eventually led to India's freedom in 1947.
  • EM Forster's Literary Style
    • Forster's writing is known for its exploration of human relationships and the social structures that impact them.
    • He often addressed themes of class, politics, and personal growth in his works.
    • His narrative style is characterized by a blend of realism and symbolism, making his novels both engaging and thought-provoking.
    • Forster was also a member of the Bloomsbury Group, a circle of influential English writers, intellectuals, and artists.
  • Themes in "A Passage to India"
    • The novel deals with the theme of friendship and the complexities of relationships between the British colonizers and the Indian population.
    • It explores the theme of cultural misunderstanding and the struggles for mutual understanding and respect.
    • The novel also delves into the spiritual and mystical aspects of Indian culture, contrasting it with the materialism of the British.
    • It is considered a critique of British imperialism and a reflection on the possibility of genuine human connection across cultural divides.
  • Impact of "A Passage to India"
    • The novel was widely acclaimed and became a significant work in English literature.
    • It has been adapted into various stage plays and a successful film directed by David Lean in 1984.
    • The book continues to be studied in academic circles for its literary merit and historical significance.
    • It remains a poignant commentary on colonialism and its effects on both the colonizers and the colonized.

  • 'New Lamps For Old ' (1893) was written by Aurbindo Ghosh in 'Indu - Prakash', a Bombay daily newspaper.
  • Aurobindo Ghosh is also known as the Father of Indian Extremism.
  • K. G. Deshpande, a friend from his Cambridge days, was in charge of a weekly published from Bombay called Induprakash.
  • K. G. Deshpande requested Sri Aurobindo to write something on the current political situation of India.
  • Sri Aurobindo began writing a series of fiery articles titled 'New Lamps for Old', strongly criticizing the Congress, then the main political party in India, for its moderate policy.

questions.question: Which of the following novels was written by George Orwell?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following novels was written by George Orwell?
questions.solution: Animal Farm is a novel written by George Orwell, first published in 1945 as a satirical allegory of Soviet totalitarianism. The story depicts a farm where animals overthrow their human farmer to create an equal society, but it ultimately explores themes of power, corruption, and betrayal. George Orwell, born Eric Arthur Blair, was an English novelist known for his lucid prose, social criticism, and opposition to totalitarianism. His notable works, including Animal Farm and 1984, have had a profound influence on culture and political thought, with terms like "Orwellian" emerging from his work.
